text:
maya: Heads up — during the v4.2 canary we're seeing tail latency jump ~3-5x on a subset of hosts after the tokenizer change. KV cache miss rate on those hosts goes from ~6% -> 28%.

jonathan: ugh. is this across all models or just the canary variant?

maya: only the canary model (tokenizer: split-on-emoji change). traffic skewed to shorter utterances but with more token boundaries. repro on canary hosts, not on control.

li: do we have kernel selection logs? might be falling back to generic kernels for short seqs and tiny batches.

maya: attaching profiler snippet from one host (relevant lines):
```
[2026-03-17T14:02:33Z] kernel_select: chosen=generic_attn, score=0.12, fallback_reason=small_batch
[2026-03-17T14:02:34Z] kv_cache: miss_rate=0.28, avg_prefix_tokens=4.2
[2026-03-17T14:02:35Z] batcher: observed_batch_size=2.1, batching_window_ms=12
[2026-03-17T14:02:36Z] p99_latency_ms=620
```

ryan: that looks like the tokenizer increased token counts but made prefixes shorter (more boundary tokens), so KV cache prefix reuse goes down -> more full-attn work. small batch sizes also push us to generic kernels.

anika: can we force kernel selection to prefer the optimized small-seq kernel so it doesn't fall back? or tune batching_window?

li: we can bump batching_window to 20ms for the canary pool as a quick experiment. also we should capture perf counters per-request (kv_hits, chosen_kernel) for deeper analysis.

maya: rolling patch to adjust batching window on canary now. deploy-bot: "canary rollout paused due to latency anomaly"

deploy-bot: Canary pause acknowledged — automatic health checks flagged 3/10 hosts.

jonathan: while we test batching, we should also check tokenizer output distribution. maya — can you dump token length histogram for recent traffic?

maya: pasted token histogram (last 30m):
```
0-2 tokens: 12%
3-6 tokens: 58%
7-15 tokens: 25%
>15 tokens: 5%
median=5 tokens, mean=6.1
previous-control-median=9 tokens
```

ryan: yep median dropped a lot. that explains small batches and poor kv reuse.

anika: quick mitigation options: 1) revert tokenizer patch in canary 2) increase batching window + enable prefix aggregation heuristic 3) force optimized kernel affinity for small-seq until we stabilize.

li: preference 2 then 3, because reverting loses the emoji handling test we want in canary. but we should keep 1 as fallback if perf doesn't recover.

maya: bumping window to 25ms and enabling prefix aggregation on canary hosts now.

sre-bot: Sampling profiler started on host r-i-004 for 60s; trace id=trace-1802506795

jonathan: any improvement numbers?

maya: after change (10m): p99 down from 620ms -> 150ms on canary hosts; kv miss rate back to ~9%; observed_batch_size increased 2.1 -> 6.8.

ryan: nice. kernel_select logs show optimized_small_attn being chosen again.

anika: let's keep the tokenizer change in canary but update default batching configs for pools with median seq <= 8. file a follow-up to make batching config dynamic by seq-distribution.

li: filed ENG-3421 for dynamic-batching-by-seq (owner: li). linked traces and profiler.

maya: leaving canary paused for another hour for monitor. will resume rollout when stable for 30m. thanks all. :thumbsup:
